newsitem.title: USA: Citizens panel sets hearings on LIPA's LILCO offer.
newsitem.headline: Citizens panel sets hearings on LIPA's LILCO offer.

text.p: The Citizens Advisory Panel has asked the Long Island Power Authority to postpone its vote on a partial take over of Long Island Lighting Co until formal evidentiary hearings can be held, CAP's executive director, Gordian Raacke, said Monday.
The panel is a watchdog group appointed by the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York to advise the public on LILCO issues, Raacke said.
In a letter to LIPA Chairman Richard Kessel, the group "demanded that LIPA postpone its scheduled vote set for Monday, June 16," at 1600 EDT/2000 GMT.
LIPA has scheduled a vote on a definitive agreement with LILCO, Raacke said.
LIPA spokesman Seth Hulkower pointed out the authority never releases its agenda before meeting.

Following approval by LIPA, the agreement goes to the Public Authority Control Board -- composed of New York's governor, Senate majority leader and Assembly speaker -- where it needs unanimous approval.
Kessel is scheduled to make his promised appearance before the Assembly Energy Committee in Albany tomorrow, Raacke said.
This is expected to be the committee's final hearing on LIPA's proposed partial takeover of LILCO.
It was scheduled to allow Kessel a chance to respond to statements made at the earlier sessions.
In a statement, CAP said its repeated requests that LIPA conduct an evidentiary process were rebuffed by the authority.

An evidentiary process includes pre-filed testimony by expert witnesses, formal discovery and cross-examination of expert witnesses before an independent hearing officer who would prepare a written recommendation, the group explained.
"Since LIPA continues to refuse to provide for this essential fact finding process, CAP feels obligated to conduct such hearings to protect ratpayers' interests," Raacke said.

In the letter to LIPA, the executive director said "There are many unanswered questions and criticisms of the LIPA-LILCO deal. (CAP's) consultants have concluded that the proposed partial takeover of LILCO is a bad deal for ratepayers. This conclusion is vastly differenct from that of (LIPA's) consultants. The best way to sourt out the truth of this matter is through an evidentiary process."

Hulkower said CAP spent nearly two hours presenting testimony at last Wednesday's LIPA meeting, adding the authority believes it has "taken ample public comment" to proceed with a vote if decides this is warranted.

CAP's letter also pointed out that "the work of the Suffolk County Legislature's consultants concerning the deal has yet to be completed and the alternative proposal to the LIPA-LILCO deal being developed by the Initiative for Competitive Energy is not finalized and made public.
Raacke noted the Energy Committee's sessions were public statement hearings with no formal cross-examination.

CAP was formed as a result of the settlement LILCO reached after a jury found it guilty of misrepresentations in a RICO case filed in conjunction with construction of the Shoreham nuclear power plant.
The settlement called for LILCO to refund $400 million to ratepayers over a ten year period ending in about two years and fund CAP to monitor the utility's compliance with the agreement.

Raacke said the panel believes the proposal before LIPA contains two violations of the RICO settlement, funding the upfront rebate to ratepayers with money they were to get anyway under the settlement and allowing LILCO to keep some of the funds scheduled to be paid out under the settlement.
If the LIPA proposal is not changed, he said, the group plans to appeal it to the federal court "the moment they start to implement it." ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
